title: Cohort Latency-Regulated Release Adjudicator
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Design and implement a policy adjudicator that uses cohort-level latency signals to regulate staged canary releases. The adjudicator will dynamically adjust step schedules and traffic splits, trigger shadow probing across cohorts, and perform safe auto-rollback when latency regressions or failed probes are detected.
background: Current rollout tooling supports static step schedules and percentage-based traffic splits with basic telemetry gates. We need a more adaptive engine that reasons about cohort heterogeneity (e.g., mobile vs desktop), transient noise, and correlated latency regressions. This ticket covers the policy component that decides whether to advance, hold, reduce traffic, or roll back based on cohort-aware latency windows and probe results.
proposal: Implement a Cohort Latency-Regulated Release Adjudicator (CLRA) that consumes per-cohort latency histograms, error rates, and active shadow probe outcomes. Key capabilities: 1) cohort-aware step eligibility: require each critical cohort to meet percentile SLOs for a configurable window; 2) adaptive step-sizing: automatically increase or decrease next-step traffic by bucketed multipliers instead of fixed increments; 3) shadow probing integration: run active probes in parallel during holds and surface probe failures; 4) conservative auto-rollback: require sustained violation across a quorum of cohorts or a single severe regression before rolling back; 5) declarative policy DSL for PMs to express tolerances and weightings.
acceptance_criteria: CLRA evaluates cohort data and emits a deterministic decision (advance/hold/scale-down/rollback) for any given rollout state
End-to-end unit and integration tests cover noisy signals, transient spikes, and gradual regressions
Can be attached to existing rollout orchestrator via a stable gRPC decision API
Dashboard surfaces per-cohort decision rationale and contributing metrics for at least 7 days
Automatic rollback can be disabled per-release and audited in the console
implementation_notes: Phase 1: implement core adjudicator logic in the release service; include a pluggable scoring function for cohorts. Phase 2: add shadow probe runner and probe result ingestion. Phase 3: expose DSL in console and add UI for adjustments. Use existing telemetry stream (metrics-kafka) and store short-term sliding windows in the adjudicator's Redis cache for fast evaluation. Rollout decisions must be idempotent and versioned with the release manifest.
rollout_plan: Start with an internal dogfood release for the infra team: 1) enable CLRA in dry-run mode for 2 weeks (decisions logged but not enforced); 2) run controlled canary for a low-risk model with small cohorts; 3) enable enforcement with a strict hold-on-fail policy for 1 month; 4) expand to standard model releases once monitoring and rollback telemetry are verified.
telemetry_and_guardrails: Track per-cohort p50/p90/p99 latencies, error rate, 95th percentile tail latency delta vs baseline, probe pass rate, and decision latency. Guardrails: enforce max traffic jump per step (configurable default 2x), minimum observation window (default 5 minutes), and decision cool-down (default 3 minutes). Emit structured decision events including contributing metrics and policy version.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert when adjudicator decision latency > 10s (SLO breach)
Alert if >1% of decisions in the last hour choose rollback for minor regressions (indicator of flapping)
Runbook: follow auto-rollback investigation doc and revert policy definitions if needed
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy cohort signals cause premature rollbacks — Mitigation: require quorum or sustained regression window before rollback
Risk: high decision latency impacting release throughput — Mitigation: cache pre-aggregated cohort stats and ensure decision engine is horizontally scalable
Risk: policy complexity leads to operator errors — Mitigation: provide safe defaults, a dry-run mode, and an explanation UI
